description: Is the cluster absorbing writes or falling behind? Ordered cause to symptom: offered load, thread pool saturation, blocked tasks, dropped messages, hints, compaction backlog, client errors.

panels.description: Coordinator-side write rate per node. Everything below answers whether the cluster is absorbing this rate or falling behind it.
panels.title: Write Throughput

panels.description: Per-node write latency at the selected percentile. These gauges are pre-aggregated on each node and are never summed or averaged together.
panels.title: Write Latency ${percentile} (${latency_unit:text})

panels.description: All four percentiles together, independent of the Percentile variable. Backpressure shows first in the tail: p999 and max move well before p50 does.
panels.title: Write Latency Ladder — p50 / p99 / p999 / max (${latency_unit:text})
Saturation — thread pools show it first

panels.description: Queued tasks by pool. This is the earliest signal that the cluster is not keeping up; it moves before drops and before hints.
panels.title: Thread Pool Pending — top 8

panels.description: MutationStage, ReadStage and RequestResponseStage. Active at the pool ceiling with pending above zero means the pool, not the disk, is the limit.
panels.title: Request Pools — active tasks

panels.description: Tasks the pool refused to queue. Distinct from pending: pending is a queue, blocked is real backpressure applied to the caller. Any sustained non-zero value here is significant.
panels.title: Blocked Task Rate — top 8

panels.description: Flush writers, post-flush and reclaim. A backlog here holds memory and eventually blocks the mutation stage.
panels.title: Memtable Flush Pipeline — pending

panels.description: Messages discarded after exceeding their timeout. Zero is the healthy reading; any non-zero series here means work was thrown away.
panels.title: Dropped Messages by Type — top 10

panels.description: Two different failures. A dropped mutation is data the cluster accepted and did not apply, so it must be repaired. A dropped read is only a failed request.
panels.title: Dropped Mutations vs Dropped Reads
Symptom — hints mean a peer is down or slow

panels.description: Hints currently being stored or replayed. A rise means a replica is not accepting writes.
panels.title: Hints In Progress

panels.description: New hints per second. Sustained accrual with nothing in progress means hints are being written as fast as they are replayed.
panels.title: Hint Accrual Rate

panels.description: The pool that replays hints back to the recovered peer. Pending work here delays consistency.
panels.title: Hints Dispatcher — active and pending
Backlog — compaction is the slowest thing to recover

panels.description: Pending tasks on the left axis, completions per second on the right. Writes that outrun compaction raise the SSTable count, which then shows up as read latency on the Read Path dashboard.
panels.title: Compaction Backlog vs Completion Rate

panels.description: Bytes of live data per node. Compare the slope with the compaction completion rate on the left.
panels.title: Storage Load per Node

panels.description: unavailable means not enough replicas answered, timeout means they were too slow, failure means a replica returned an error. Each points somewhere different.
panels.title: Client Errors by Status

panels.description: Total errors accumulated across the dashboard time range, by operation and status.
panels.title: Errors over the selected range

list.description: Which pre-aggregated latency gauge to read. The gauges are computed per node; they are never summed or averaged across nodes.
list.label: Percentile
list.name: percentile

list.description: Display unit for latency. The metric is emitted in microseconds, so the value is the divisor: milliseconds divides by 1000, microseconds divides by 1.
list.label: Latency unit
list.name: latency_unit

list.description: Database nodes only. Derived from a Cassandra-only metric, so control and app nodes never appear.
list.label: Host
list.name: host

title: Write Path Backpressure
